extracted.intended_audience: news editors (AP clients) and general news readers
extracted.subtask_description: Associated press (AP) wire copy and front‑page news dispatches demonstrating dateline/byline formats, embargo/advance markings, lead labeling, and concise lede reporting for distribution to newspapers and broadcasters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline format (city, date, AP tag)
rubrics_metrics.description: Datelines appear as 'CITY, COUNTRY/STATE, FEB. 12 (AP)-' preceding the story (e.g., 'BELGRADE, YUGOSLAVIA, FEB. 12 (AP)-', 'WASHINGTON, FEB. 12 (AP)-').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the city (and country/state where relevant), the date, and the parenthetical source tag '(AP)' followed by a dash before the lead sentence. This format signals story origin and source to editors and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Byline format
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporter attribution appears as a byline such as 'BY ALEX He SINGLETON', 'BY JOHN RODERICK', 'BY MARVIN ARROWSMITH'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place a clear byline with 'BY' and the reporter's name near the top of the story to credit the author and enable routing/assignment. The examples show uppercase/line placement typical of wire copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance / embargo markings and timestamps
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories include explicit embargo/usage instructions like 'ADVANCE FOR USE AT 6 P.M. EST SATURDAY, FEB. 12' and 'END ADVANCE FOR USE AT 7 PM EST SATURDAY FEB. 12'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a story is not for immediate release, label it 'ADVANCE' and give the exact local time and date for permitted use; optionally mark when the advance period ends. These markings are instructions to subscribing editors for timing publication or broadcast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal lead/section labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Short internal labels such as 'NIGHT_LEAD', 'NIGHT LEAD ATOMIC', 'NIGHT_LEAD TITO', 'NIGHT LEAD NIXON' appear to tag prominent leads or assignment categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise internal labels to identify lead items, assignment types, or package positions for desk editors (e.g., night lead, regional focus, topic tag). These help in routing and placement decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise, summary lede (who/what/where/when/why)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opening sentences quickly state the main fact or event (e.g., 'PRESIDENT TITO CAUTIONED THE ... NATIONS TODAY AGAINST "STICKING THEIR NOSES" INTO INTERNAL AFFAIRS', 'THE UNITED STATES STEPPED UP ITS ATOMS-FOR-PEACE PROGRAM TODAY...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead paragraphs should summarize the essential facts — who, what, where, when and why/impact — in a clear, compact manner suitable for the inverted‑pyramid style of wire copy so editors can trim from the bottom if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source tagging and parenthetical source attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Parenthetical tags like '(AP)' are used repeatedly to indicate the news agency source at dateline and within items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistently tag agency copy with the proper source parenthetical to preserve attribution and allow editors and readers to identify origin quickly. This is part of wire distribution standards.
